title: Atlas and Regiment
premise: In 1898, in the pearl-trading port of Saltmere Bay, Lior Winterbourne has spent his life believing history is something that happens elsewhere. When a sealed letter arrives naming his family as heirs to a disputed shipping charter, the powerful Meridian Trading Company moves to erase them, and Lior discovers his indenture was designed to keep him silent. Torn between the company that owns his debt and a promise made years ago to Sable Ashkani, now declared an enemy of the crown, he must smuggle her aboard the morning tide ship before the company's agents close in. He succeeds at terrible cost — losing his name, his papers, and nearly his life — but gains the belonging he always believed history would never offer him.
about_author: Lior Ravensworth grew up among the dockyards of a fading port town, listening to sailors' half-true histories. A former archivist, they write novels about ordinary people caught in the machinery of empire.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Lior dives for pearls to pay down his family's indenture to Meridian Trading, convinced history belongs to admirals and merchants, not divers like him. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking a hunger for a larger life.

chapters.title: A Letter in Wax
chapters.summary: A solicitor delivers a sealed letter naming the Winterbournes as claimants to an old shipping charter. Lior's mother burns it unread; Lior secretly keeps a scrap. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: first crack in his belief that his family stands outside history.

chapters.title: The Company's Kindness
chapters.summary: Meridian's factor, Mr. Corvane, offers to forgive the family's entire debt — if they renounce all claims and sign silence papers. His generosity feels like a trap closing. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: dread dressed as gratitude.

chapters.title: What Sable Promised
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: years earlier, young Lior promised Sable Ashkani, daughter of a rival trading house, that if she ever needed passage out of Saltmere Bay, he'd get her aboard any ship, any tide. POV: alternating Lior and Sable. Emotional beat: warmth of a vow made when the world was simpler.

chapters.title: Declared Enemy
chapters.summary: War rumors break; the Ashkani house is branded treasonous, their assets seized. Sable returns to Saltmere Bay in disguise, calling in Lior's promise. The morning tide ship sails in three days. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Indentured Silence
chapters.summary: Lior learns his indenture contract contains a clause binding him to report 'persons of interest' — Sable by name. Corvane reveals he knows she's back; the letter was bait all along. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: betrayal, then fury at being made a tool of power.

chapters.title: The Diver's Route
chapters.summary: Lior plans escape through the flooded sea-caves only divers know, bribing a harbor pilot with his mother's last pearl. Corvane doubles the watch on the docks. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose — he chooses whose side of history he's on.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Boats
chapters.summary: The plan unravels: the pilot betrays them, Corvane's men corner Lior and Sable in the caves as the tide rises. Lior nearly drowns holding the passage open. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, trust, and the truth that belonging demands risk.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Wounded and half-drowned, Lior gets Sable aboard the departing ship as Corvane arrives too late. Lior refuses to board with her, staying to face the company and shield his family. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief and fierce clarity — keeping the promise costs him everything but himself.

chapters.title: The Charter and the Child
chapters.summary: Corvane falls when the forged provenance of the charter surfaces; the Winterbourne claim, kept alive by the burned letter's surviving scrap, restores the family's freedom. Years later, Lior — a free man telling his daughter about tides — receives a letter from across the sea. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: resolution — memory kept, power answered, belonging earned.
